title: How to put a cartoon character into a real video with AI
summary: Put an original or licensed cartoon character into real video with Magic Hour. Prepare the reference and footage, generate a short test, and review common failure points.
body_markdown:
Quick Answer


## Quick answer


To put a cartoon character into a real video, upload the source footage and a clear character reference to[Magic Hour's Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) . Start with a short, well-lit clip, then inspect identity, movement, hands, occlusion, shadows and background stability. Use an original character or one you are authorized to upload and publish.

This guide covers subject replacement. Character Replace uses an existing performance and a reference image; it is different from restyling the whole shot or animating a still image.


### Put your character into a real video


Start with a short, well-lit shot and one clear original or licensed character reference. Review identity, hands, occlusion, shadows, background and frame-to-frame stability before using the result.


[Try Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace)


## What you need


-


**A source video:** one continuous shot with a clearly visible primary subject.


-


**A character reference:** a sharp image that clearly shows the intended cartoon, mascot, anime or illustrated character.


-


**Permission:** rights to upload the source footage and reference and to use the output for the intended purpose.


-


**A review plan:** the specific identity, scene and motion details that must remain stable.


## Prepare a useful cartoon reference


Use a clean image with the character clearly visible and minimally obstructed. A simple background, readable silhouette and visible face and body give the system less irrelevant information to interpret.


For a brand or commercial project, the clearest route is an original mascot or a properly licensed character. If you do not have one, create a reference with[Magic Hour's AI Image Generator](https://magichour.ai/products/ai-image-generator) and keep the accepted prompt and source files with the project.


Avoid using a famous character merely because a preset or reference is technically available. Tool access does not establish your right to publish that character in an ad, product or monetized video.


## Prepare the source video


-


**Start short.** A short sample makes failures faster and cheaper to diagnose before processing a longer sequence.


-


**Keep the subject visible.** Heavy occlusion gives the model fewer frames in which to maintain the replacement.


-


**Prefer one continuous shot.** Fast cuts change lighting, scale and camera geometry abruptly.


-


**Reduce blur and darkness.** Motion blur and low light obscure the subject boundaries and reference details.


-


**Use the final crop.** Test in the aspect ratio and framing you plan to publish.


## How to put a cartoon character into a real video


### 1. Open Character Replace


Open[Character Replace](https://magichour.ai/products/character-replace) . The current public workflow asks for a video and a reference image and also offers sample references for testing.


### 2. Add the source video


Upload the real footage containing the person or character to replace. Use the shortest representative section first, especially when the full video contains cuts, occlusion or lighting changes.


### 3. Add the cartoon reference


Upload the original or licensed character image. Match the source subject's visible angle and body coverage when possible; a face-only reference provides less information for a full-body replacement.


### 4. Generate one sample


Generate the clip using the current Replace mode. For an automated pipeline, the[Character Replace API](https://docs.magichour.ai/api-reference/video-projects/character-replace) accepts video and image assets, start and end times, resolution, mode and selection settings. Check the live product or API estimate instead of relying on historical credit or timing figures.


### 5. Review the entire result


-


**Identity:** does the character remain recognizable from the first frame to the last?


-


**Motion:** do pose, body movement, timing and camera movement still follow the source?


-


**Boundaries:** inspect hands, hair, clothing edges and moments when objects cross the subject.


-


**Scene:** look for changed backgrounds, shadows, reflections or nearby objects.


-


**Continuity:** pause around fast movement and cuts to find flicker or sudden shape changes.


If one issue dominates, change one input at a time. Try a clearer reference for identity drift, brighter or less blurred footage for unstable boundaries, or a shorter continuous section when cuts cause discontinuity.


## What the current product documents


As checked September 13, 2026, Magic Hour documents real and stylized references, including cartoons, anime and illustrations. The product page says Character Replace is designed to preserve the source timing, body movement, poses, camera movement and scene while changing the primary subject. It also warns that low light, motion blur, heavy occlusion and fast cuts can contribute to flicker or drift.


Treat those statements as intended product behavior, not a guarantee for every clip. The source and reference determine how much usable information the model receives, and every output still needs full-video review.


## What to do after the character replacement


Use[Lip Sync](https://magichour.ai/products/lip-sync) when the character must follow new speech. Use[Video-to-Video](https://magichour.ai/products/video-to-video) when the goal is to restyle the complete shot rather than change only the primary subject. Keep each transformation as a separate step so you can identify which stage introduced a problem.
